tool_arguments.prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Asset: reusable production key-pose sprite sheet for a children's educational video. Freshly redraw ONE transparent square RGBA sheet containing exactly NINE complete full-body poses of the SAME animal from image1 in a precise 3 by 3 row-major grid. Highest available native resolution, aiming at 3072 square or at least 2048. Image1 is the fixed adopted identity/style/proportions reference ONLY, not a pixel-edit target. Every cell has one whole subject with ample clear transparent margins, no overlap, labels, grid lines, borders, floor, shadow, background, props, clothing, text, effects, sparkles, or extra animals. Match the exact warm brown outlines, clean soft watercolor paper texture, palette, face and eye design, markings, appendages, and body proportions in image1. Keep ONE shared head size, torso size, body scale and relative support baseline across all nine poses. Never enlarge bent poses or shorten the torso. The first blink pose MUST reproduce the ordinary reference stance, head/torso ratio, torso length/thickness and foot or body-centre position, with ONLY eyelids changing. No squat, larger head, lowered skull, lifted resting arms or shorter belly in blink. Closed eyes are simple relaxed brown curves; open eyes retain exactly the reference format, with no new eye highlights. All other poses retain that same body scale. Keep attachments and complete parts clear, without doubled limbs, clipped extremities, pigment smears, ragged halos or stray marks. Intentional paper grain is subtle, not dirty pigment patches. Subject: Steller Sea Lion (トド). Identity details to retain: 黄褐色の丸い頭胴・長めの前フリッパー・後フリッパー. The animal remains the reference's simplified nonhumanoid animal prop. Keep its exact existing bird/fish/marine body plan and projection, simple broad color blocks, dot-eye format where adopted, and limited feather/fin linework. Never invent human hands, arms, legs, lips, eyebrows, clothes or large anime eyes. Fish remain floating animals with existing fins and tails, no foot support invented. Grounded birds keep their existing paired feet. Steller sea lion retains its resting flipper projection. ROW-MAJOR ORDER: 1 BLINK: same reference stance/projection and body proportions, visible eye gently closed as a simple curve; all body parts at rest. 2 GREET: a small greeting using the existing near wing/fin/flipper or a gentle head lift, no new limb. 3 PRESENT LEFT: naturally direct head/bill/gaze or existing near wing/fin toward viewer LEFT, keep whole existing anatomy. 4 PRESENT RIGHT: naturally direct head/bill/gaze or existing near wing/fin toward viewer RIGHT; preserve real asymmetric markings, no mechanical mirrored duplicate. 5 THINK: subtle curious head/bill tilt down or poised head inclination, existing appendages relaxed. 6 AHA: gentle alert head lift and small existing appendage lift, simple friendly dot eye, no effects. 7 CHEER: pleased small existing wing/fin/flipper lift, stable same body size and support/centre; do not add a human mouth. 8 SPECIES A: A gentle small lift of one reference-visible foreflipper, keeping the same resting body projection and support. 9 SPECIES B: The same foreflipper lowers part-way toward its original position; preserve the rear flipper shapes and body scale. Species-specific constraints: 前びれを人の手へ変えない。後端を新しい足・尾として二重に描かず、既存の支点種別に従う。 No extra neutral frame. Full uncut transparent padding around the entire animal in every cell. Deliver finished clear child-friendly illustration, not a contact sheet with words.
